newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT soars to two-year high on peso fears.
newsitem.headline: PLDT soars to two-year high on peso fears.

text.p: Shares of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) climbed to a two-year high on Friday and other firms with large export earnings followed suit as talk of the peso weakening over the next few days swirled in the market.

"Investors are hedging that with a potential depreciation or devaluation of the peso, PLDT and other issues with foreign-denominated earnings will benefit," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
International calls account for about 50 percent of PLDT's revenue.
The firm's shares gained 60 pesos, or 6.9 percent, on Friday and closed at its intra-day high of 930 pesos, emerging as the most actively traded issue for the day.
"I guess they (investors) are betting on a depreciation of the peso but, of course, its American Depositary Receipt (ADR) helped," said Ramon Saulo, senior analyst at Asiamerit Securities.
PLDT's ADR climbed $1 1/4 on Thursday to $65 3/8.
A one percent depreciation of the peso would translate to a 1.72 peso gain in PLDT's earnings per share, Saulo said.
However, Guoco Securities said a one percent depreciation would mean a 1.8 peso increase in EPS.
Talk of the Philippine currency being overvalued started after Thailand on Wednesday adopted a managed float policy for the baht, a move seen as a de facto devaluation.
The baht's fall put pressure on the peso and the Philippine central bank was forced to defend it by sharply raising its overnight interest rates and buying tens of millions pesos.
It also triggered renewed calls from exporters that the government let the peso depreciate to make their products more competitive. The demand was rejected by the central bank.
Analysts said a depreciation of the peso would lead to an upgrade of PLDT's earnings for the year.
"It will be a blessing in disguise for PLDT. Even if the approval of their rate restructuring, which includes a metered pricing scheme gets delayed, their earnings will not be affected," said Mejia.

Sun Hung Kai Securities vice-president for research Raul Ruiz said his 6.26 billion pesos net income forecast for PLDT in 1997 had already taken into account a 3.5 percent depreciation to 27.2 pesos per dollar by the end of the year.
On Friday, the peso was quoted at 26.399 to the dollar.

Although blue-chip PLDT is the most prominent beneficiary of the peso depreciation talk, traders said share prices of other export-oriented issues, including gold producer Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co and electronics exporter Ionics Circuits Inc also surged.
Ionics closed 1.50 peso higher at 16.25 pesos, while Lepanto gained one centavo to 60 centavos.
If the peso depreciates, shares of firms with heavy imports and those with large foreign debt would fall.
Oil refiner Petron Corp imported large amounts of crude oil, while brewer San Miguel Corp had large foreign borrowings, Ruiz said.
